title: Add Codex Cloud workflow entry point foundation
objective: Allow a terminal workflow step to reference a preconfigured Codex Cloud environment behind a durable provider gateway without making ADT a repository automation engine.
userContext: A maintainer wants the final workflow step to hand an exact prepared task to Codex Cloud and eventually receive the pull request created with Codex's own GitHub integration.
currentBehaviour: WF-001 and WF-002 provide durable orchestration and encrypted text-provider connections, but no separate Codex Cloud execution surface.
requiredBehaviour: Add safe D1 environment references, constrained Codex agent options, a CodexCloudGateway, deterministic mock lifecycle, durable coding-complete and publication stages, terminal-only validation, cancellation semantics, UI, and a production connection that fails closed while transport is unavailable.
userExperience: Connections clearly reports Transport unavailable, maintainers can manage safe environment references, and run details distinguish coding from pull-request publication and prioritize the final pull-request URL.
functionalRequirements: Compose the agent master prompt and byte-exact workflow input deterministically.
Persist a returned task ID before polling and never restart an attempt that has one.
Persist coding output and task URL before pull-request publication.
Treat a Codex step as successful only after structured pull-request metadata is available.
Keep codex-cloud separate from openai-responses and allow it only as the final workflow step.
Store only a safe environment key, display name, external environment ID, and enabled flag.
technicalConsiderations: Official Codex documentation was reviewed on 2026-08-08. No documented server-to-server API contract covering environment task creation, stable task retrieval, result and PR metadata, publication, and cancellation was available; Path B is therefore required.
Real Codex Cloud execution is unavailable until OpenAI exposes a supported server-to-server Codex Cloud transport that satisfies the gateway contract.
Codex owns repository checkout, environment setup, secrets, commands, tests, GitHub identity, and PR creation; ADT never receives the repository GitHub credential.
Do not use Responses, browser sessions, undocumented endpoints, GitHub issue comments, arbitrary endpoints, or arbitrary headers as a substitute transport.
outOfScope: Production Codex Cloud execution before a supported transport exists.
ADT-managed repositories, GitHub credentials, setup scripts, environment secrets, commands, branches, patches, diffs, merge, deployment, CI waiting, or post-PR steps.
Multiple Codex steps, nonterminal Codex steps, loops, branching, parallelism, swarms, or live provider requests in CI.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment references are D1-backed and contain no repository credentials or arbitrary configuration.
The gateway mock proves exact prompt construction, one start, replay polling, coding persistence, publication, cancellation, and PR URL completion without live traffic.
Ambiguous start or publication cannot automatically duplicate repository-writing work.
Connections and specifications state that production transport is intentionally unavailable.
WF-001 and WF-002 regression tests continue to pass.
codexGuidance: Implement Path B only. Preserve the security boundary and deterministic orchestration; do not infer or reverse-engineer a Codex transport and do not interact with zailghe3/fpo-artifacts.
